title: The Air Force retreats from studying China
gist: The Air Force has decided to shut down the China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI), announced Sept. 22, which will close once its civilians depart — a move the Washington Examiner frames as evidence Washington is woefully unprepared for a new Cold War with China.

themes.theme: Closure of China Aerospace Studies Institute

insights.claim: On Sept. 22 the China Aerospace Studies Institute announced the Air Force had decided to shut it down; it will finish reports in the pipeline but close once all its civilians depart.
insights.speaker: Washington Examiner
insights.so_what: Reduced in-house US analytical capacity on Chinese aerospace and military power.
insights.quote: once all the civilians eventually depart, CASI will close.

themes.theme: US unpreparedness for a China Cold War

insights.claim: The United States is in a new Cold War with communist China, an even more dangerous adversary than before, yet Washington is woefully unprepared to counter Beijing.
insights.speaker: Washington Examiner
insights.so_what: Frames sustained US-China strategic rivalry as the baseline for defence and policy spending.
insights.quote: But Washington is woefully unprepared to counter Beijing.

themes.theme: Cutting China expertise as a strategic error

insights.claim: Shutting down the Air Force's dedicated China research institute signals a retreat from studying China at the moment the rivalry intensifies, implying a self-inflicted intelligence gap.
insights.speaker: Washington Examiner
insights.so_what: Watch for congressional pushback or shifts of China analysis to contractors and think tanks.
